# Reception Perception: The Show — 2024-03-19

**Raw transcript:** `raw/ingested/reception-perception/2024-03-19-rp-weekend-receiver-news-keenan-allen-joins-bears-bills-add-curtis-samuel.md` (immutable — do not edit)

## Summary

Matt Harmon and co-host James Koh (not tracked) devote the full episode to two
free-agency stories, an unusually narrow format for the show (normally covers
many more players).

**Keenan Allen traded to the Chicago Bears.** The hosts reconstruct why the
Chargers moved on (Allen declined a pay cut at age 32, unlike Joey Bosa and
Khalil Mack, who restructured), praise Allen for handling it "like a
businessman," and grade the return (a 4th-round pick) as a shock relative to
his standing with the franchise. Harmon's charted read on Allen's 2023 season:
career highs in catches/yards, but a role deliberately narrowed toward
high-percentage underneath routes as his man-coverage separation has eroded
with age — not a declining player so much as a differently-deployed one. The
Bears pairing with [[D.J. Moore]] is graded as an excellent high-low fit for
a rookie quarterback (Caleb Williams, presumed). Extended discussion of the
Chargers' resulting receiver room (worst in the NFL, per the hosts), the
[[Justin Fields]]-to-Pittsburgh trade compensation (hosts disagree on value),
and free-agent fits for [[Mike Williams]] (Bills/Panthers/Steelers/Jets).

**Curtis Samuel signs with Buffalo** (3 years, $24M). The bulk of the episode
is Harmon making a data-backed case, off four seasons of Reception Perception
charting, that Samuel has been a consistently strong (~75%+ success rate vs.
man coverage) receiver whose box-score output has been suppressed by poor
quarterback play and disorganized offenses (Carolina under Kyle Allen,
Washington under Eric Bieniemi) — and that reuniting with OC Joe Brady, who
got his best season out of him in 2020, sets up a real 2024 breakout. Also
covers roster fit around [[Stefon Diggs]] and [[Khalil Shakir]], and touches
on [[Nico Collins]]/[[Tank Dell]] amid Texans free-agency rumors.
